speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the pattern of these symptoms, where exactly on your body do you feel the weakness, and when did it first start?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pattern of weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest, combined with diplopia that worsens on vertical gaze, is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. REQUEST TEST: Routine_Bloods (including Creatine_Kinase and Thyroid_Function) and REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Routine_Bloods: Not performed in this session; Creatine_Kinase: Not performed in this session; Thyroid_Function: Not performed in this session.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The presence of elevated Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies, combined with your history of activity-induced weakness and vertical diplopia, confirms this diagnosis. I have ordered the necessary tests and will await the remaining blood results to finalize the workup.
